sentences.text: Feitianius stands out among its known relatives because it possessed tail plumage made of three distinct feather types.
The animal's thighbone measured exactly twenty-seven millimetres in length.
Scientists considered these tail feathers unlikely to have served an important aerodynamic function.
A team of seven researchers, including Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor, named and described the genus in 2015.
The name Feitianius honors the feitian, a flying nymph from Buddhist mythology.
In 2016, the species was placed within the Enantiornithes.
It belongs to the parent group known as the Enantiornithes.
This creature lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
